'''Andreas Sebastian Weigend''' (born 1961) is a German-American computer scientist and author of the book ''Data for the People'' (Basic Books, 2017). He was a member of Germany's Digital Council under Merkel, ''Digitalrat''.<ref>{{cite web|title=Prominenter Abgang in Merkels Digitalrat|periodical=Capital.de|publisher=|url=https://www.capital.de/wirtschaft-politik/prominenter-abgang-in-merkels-digitalrat|url-status=|format=|access-date=|archive-url=|archive-date=|last=Thomas Steinmann|date=2020-02-18|language=|pages=|quote=}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=2006-02-08 |title=Music in the Digital Age: An Interview with MusicStrands' Andreas Weigend |url=https://knowledge.wharton.upenn.edu/article/music-in-the-digital-age-an-interview-with-musicstrands-andreas-weigend/ |access-date=2026-10-24 |website=Knowledge at Wharton}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Bent |first=Adam |date=2025-10-20 |title=Andreas Weigend: Shaping Human-Centered Data Strategy and AI Through Insight and Collaboration |url=https://www.ibtimes.com/andreas-weigend-shaping-human-centered-data-strategy-ai-through-insight-collaboration-3787686 |access-date=2026-10-24 |website=International Business Times |language=en-US}}</ref>

Weigend studied physics and philosophy at the [[University of Bonn]] and received a PhD in physics from [[Stanford University]] in 1991. He was the Chief Scientist at [[Amazon.com]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Amazon Empire |url=https://www.pbs.org/wgbh/frontline/documentary/amazon-empire/transcript/ |website=Frontline |publisher=PBS}}</ref>

=== Early life and education ===
Weigend studied electrical engineering before pursuing studies in physics and philosophy at Karlsruhe, Cambridge and Bonn. In 1983, he was a summer student at [[CERN]]. He later received a doctorate in physics from [[Stanford University]].<ref>{{Cite news |last=Wagner |first=Thomas |title=Interview - „Jeder kennt eure Daten“ |url=https://www.freitag.de/autoren/thomas-wagner/jeder-kennt-eure-daten |access-date=2026-11-11 |work=Der Freitag |language=de |issn=0945-2095}}</ref>

=== Academic and industry career ===
Weigend worked at Amazon from 2002 to 2004 as its chief scientist. During his time there, he was involved in the company's [[Management of tuberculosis|data strategy]] and research into customer behaviour.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Music in the Digital Age: An Interview with MusicStrands’ Andreas Weigend |url=https://knowledge.wharton.upenn.edu/article/music-in-the-digital-age-an-interview-with-musicstrands-andreas-weigend/ |access-date=2026-11-11 |website=Knowledge at Wharton |language=en-US}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=2006-05-22 |title=The Webolution of Retail Continues |url=https://www.destinationcrm.com/Articles/ReadArticle.aspx?ArticleID=42447 |access-date=2026-11-11 |website=CRM Magazine |language=en-US}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Andreas Weigend |url=https://dataedge.ischool.berkeley.edu/2016/speakers/andreas-weigend.html |access-date=2026-11-11 |website=DataEDGE Conference |language=en}}</ref>

=== Public service in Germany ===
In August 2018, Weigend was appointed to the German government's Digital Council, an advisory body established under Chancellor [[Angela Merkel]]. He left the council in March 2019.<ref>{{Cite web |last=NACHRICHTEN |first=n-tv |title=Ex-Amazon-Experte verließ Digitalrat |url=https://www.n-tv.de/politik/Ex-Amazon-Experte-verliess-Digitalrat-article21583945.html |access-date=2026-11-11 |website=n-tv.de |language=de}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Ärzteblatt |first=Deutscher Ärzteverlag GmbH, Redaktion Deutsches |date=2018-08-22 |title=Bundesregierung setzt Digitalrat ein |url=https://www.aerzteblatt.de/news/bundesregierung-setzt-digitalrat-ein-b926eb04-3396-4b08-b886-53a50780a8da |access-date=2026-11-11 |website=Deutsches Ärzteblatt |language=de}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=online |first=heise |date=2018-08-22 |title=Digitalrat der Bundesregierung nimmt Arbeit auf |url=https://www.heise.de/news/Digitalrat-der-Bundesregierung-nimmt-Arbeit-auf-4143227.html |access-date=2026-11-11 |website=heise online |language=de}}</ref>
